newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end up 4.26 pct on Wall St, Telebras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end up 4.26 pct on Wall St, Telebras.

text.p: Brazil stocks soared to end up 4.26 percent in Sao Paulo driven by new gains in Wall Street and a strong performance of the Telebras ADR, traders said.

Players said today's rise was to be expected as local stock prices had been prevented from keeping up with the Wall Street rally as markets remained closed Monday and Tuesday due to the Carnival break.
The Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares ended at 86,706 points, close to the day's highs and up 6,540 points against Friday's close.
"Today's was a very bullish market. Stocks needed to accumulate two day's worth of gains," said a Sao Paulo trader.

A second factor behind today's rally was the steady rise of the Telebras ADR which at the time of the Sao Paulo close was up 3.25 percent. Telebras preferred traded up 6.5 percent to end at 95.50 reais.
Players said stocks were also boosted by the general optimism following a string of successes by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's multiparty coalition in Congress.
Analysts said they were positive about the president's chances of securing a constitutional amendment that would allow him to run for a second term in office.
They were also upbeat about the government's plans to reform the civil service under a far-ranging bill which is scheduled to be voted next week.
Players said they expected the market to trade nervously over the coming days ahead of the futures settlement Thursday and the options close on Monday Feb 17.
